key_insight: Successive screenshots repeat much of the same visual content, suggesting that visual indexing need not start from scratch for every frame. StreamEmbed targets real-time screenshot retrieval by exploiting this redundancy.
problem_solved: Screen history must be encoded and indexed as screenshots arrive. OCR-based indexing loses visual information, while full visual encoding takes over two seconds, creating a bottleneck for live searchable memory.
method: Treat screenshot history as an incoming stream rather than a static, offline collection.
Exploit repeated pixels within and across screenshots to reduce redundant visual computation.
Support real-time visual indexing for screenshot retrieval; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the implementation or measured results.
impact: Efficient visual indexing could make screen history a practical searchable memory for people and AI agents, retaining information that OCR alone misses. The excerpt does not establish achieved latency or retrieval quality.

paper_title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
paper_authors: Dayoon Ko, Yichuan Wang, Soyeong Jeong, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Gunhee Kim
